note: All of NG Lightbox's state is the config object ng_lightbox.settings (patterns, default_width, lightbox_class, skip_admin_paths, renderer) edited at /admin/config/media/ng-lightbox behind the 'administer ng lightbox' permission. hook_link_alter() passes every link through the ng_lightbox service, which matches the path (and its alias) against the patterns and then adds class use-ajax, data-dialog-type (renderer minus the drupal_ prefix) and data-dialog-options {width,dialogClass}. Medium cases save real non-default config for the agent to read; hard cases are verified both against config and behaviourally by calling the live service (isNgLightboxEnabledPath / addLightbox). Shipped defaults, restored by every cleanup/reset: patterns '', default_width 700, lightbox_class '', skip_admin_paths TRUE, renderer drupal_modal.

evals.prompt: Which Drupal configuration object and key does the ng_lightbox module use to decide which paths open in a lightbox, and what is the required format for those paths?
evals.expected_output: ng_lightbox.settings, key 'patterns' — a newline-separated list of paths that must start with a leading slash, with * as the wildcard (e.g. /comment/*/reply). It is edited at /admin/config/media/ng-lightbox (permission 'administer ng lightbox') and defaults to an empty string, so nothing is lightboxed until it is set.

evals.prompt: With the Drupal ng_lightbox module, how do I make one specific link open in the lightbox without adding its path to the module's settings?
evals.expected_output: Add the CSS class 'ng-lightbox' to the anchor (e.g. '#options' => ['attributes' => ['class' => ['ng-lightbox']]]). ng_lightbox_link_alter() checks for that class as well as the configured patterns and calls NgLightbox::addLightbox() either way.

evals.prompt: What exactly does the Drupal ng_lightbox module add to a link's markup when that link matches its configuration? Name the class and the data attributes.
evals.expected_output: NgLightbox::addLightbox() adds the core class 'use-ajax', sets data-dialog-type to the configured renderer with the 'drupal_' prefix stripped (so 'modal' or 'dialog'), and sets data-dialog-options to a JSON object {"width": default_width, "dialogClass": lightbox_class}. The module also attaches its library (core/drupal.ajax) on every page.

evals.prompt: Inspect this running Drupal site: which paths does ng_lightbox currently open in a lightbox, how wide is the dialog, and are admin paths excluded?
evals.expected_output: ng_lightbox.settings has patterns "/contact" and "/node/*", default_width 900, lightbox_class empty, skip_admin_paths FALSE (so admin paths are NOT excluded) and renderer drupal_modal.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, when ng_lightbox decorates a matching link, what exact value ends up in the link's data-dialog-options attribute, and what value does data-dialog-type get? Base your answer on the site's live configuration.
evals.expected_output: The site is configured with renderer drupal_dialog, default_width 640 and lightbox_class 'eval-dialog-class', so a lightboxed link gets data-dialog-type="dialog" (the drupal_ prefix is stripped) and data-dialog-options='{"width":640,"dialogClass":"eval-dialog-class"}'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, configure NG Lightbox so that the contact page (/contact) and every page under /about/ open in a lightbox that is 1000 pixels wide and carries the CSS class promo-lightbox. Admin pages must no longer be excluded from the lightbox. Apply the settings to the live site.
evals.expected_output: ng_lightbox.settings: patterns = "/contact\n/about/*", default_width = 1000, lightbox_class = 'promo-lightbox', skip_admin_paths = FALSE. Verified in config and by asking the live ng_lightbox service whether /contact is a lightboxed path.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site uses NG Lightbox with the default modal overlay. Switch it to the non-modal Core Dialog renderer and make the dialogs 500 pixels wide, so that links the module decorates carry data-dialog-type="dialog" and a width of 500. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: ng_lightbox.settings: renderer = 'drupal_dialog' (the 'Core Dialog' option, from the ng_lightbox_renderers container parameter) and default_width = 500. Verified behaviourally: NgLightbox::addLightbox() then yields class use-ajax, data-dialog-type 'dialog' and data-dialog-options {"width":500,...}.
